You are auditing the Nxeon VPS hosting platform source at /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router + Prisma, plus a worker daemon in worker/). READ ONLY — do not edit, write, deploy, restart services, or commit. Do not create any files.

Your single focus: **anything that reports success to the customer without verifying that the thing actually happened**. The team calls this the "verification gate" problem and it is the dominant defect class in this repo. A green checkmark that proves nothing is a high-priority bug.

Systematically hunt for this pattern across these subsystems and report file:line for each instance:

1. SSL / certificates (search: ssl, certbot, acme, letsencrypt, issueCert). Does "SSL installed" get set after actually confirming a cert exists and serves, or just after firing a request?
2. Domains (app/dashboard/domains, lib/namecheap.ts, lib/namecom*, DNS record writes). Does "DNS updated"/"domain registered" verify with the registrar/resolver, or trust the API call returning 200? Note: there is known prior art where the local resolver lies about DKIM.
3. Backups & restore (worker/, search backup, snapshot, restore, vzdump). Does "backup complete" verify the archive exists and is non-empty/restorable?
4. Email hosting / mailbox creation (search mailcow, mailbox, dkim, dns).
5. The migration wizard (app/dashboard/migrate, worker/migrate-real.ts, worker/migrate*.ts). Does it report "migration complete" only after verifying the destination actually serves the site? NOTE: another agent is concurrently editing worker/migrate-real.ts — read as-is and say if it looks mid-edit.
6. "Build with AI" (app/dashboard/build), one-click apps, and app/dashboard/claude-code. Does it claim an app is deployed/ACTIVE without proving it serves?
7. Server lifecycle jobs in worker/ (provision, power on/off, reinstall, resize, delete, port-forward sync, disk expand — see lib/disk-expand.ts, which another agent is editing). Does the job get marked DONE on a fire-and-forget API call, or after polling for the real state?
8. SFTP / file manager (lib/sftp.ts, app/api/files/[serverId]) — does an upload/write report success unverified?
9. Firewall / port forwarding / networking (worker/network.ts).
10. Any toast/UI that says "success", "saved", "applied", "done", "complete" where the server action swallows errors (catch blocks that return {ok:true}, empty catch, `catch {}`, `.catch(() => {})`).

Useful greps to start: `grep -rn "catch {}\|catch (e) {}\|catch {\s*}" --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx`, `grep -rn "ok: true" lib/ app/ worker/`, `grep -rn "status.*=.*\"ACTIVE\"\|DONE" worker/`.

IMPORTANT: distinguish clearly between (a) code that has a real verification gate (the team has fixed several — do not re-report fixed ones as bugs; instead confirm they verify) and (b) code that still reports unverified success. Say which is which.

Report a ranked list: severity in business terms (what a paying customer loses), exact file:line, what the customer sees vs what is true, and the smallest fix. Return findings as text in your final message; do NOT write report files.

content.text:
All four subsystem audits are complete and I verified the top-ranked claims directly against the source. Here are the findings.

---

# Verification-gate audit — Nxeon platform

**Headline:** the team's fixes are real and, in places, exemplary — migration, one-click apps, mail rules, and the Proxmox task layer all have genuine gates and should not be re-opened. The remaining defects cluster in **backups, networking, and the cPanel-lite subsystem (websites/databases), which never received the hardening `worker/apps.ts` got.**

One load-bearing fact behind most findings: `exec()`/`execInput()` in `/opt/nxeon/lib/ssh-exec.ts:114-141` **resolve** with `{code, stdout, stderr}` — a non-zero exit does not throw. Every `await exec(...)` whose result is discarded is a silent-failure site.

---

## Tier 1 — customer loses data or access

### 1. Automatic backups can silently never exist, while the UI shows a fresh timestamp daily
`/opt/nxeon/worker/backup-schedule.ts:55-61` · `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:745-768` · `/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:979-985`

Three defects compose into the worst outcome in the repo:
- `lastAutoBackup` is stamped **at job enqueue** (line 58-61), not after the backup succeeds. I confirmed it is written nowhere else — `backupCreate` never updates it.
- `backupCreate` exitstatus-gates the vzdump task (that part is fixed) but never checks the archive **exists or is non-zero**.
- `BACKUP_CREATE` is excluded from `VM_STATE_FAILURE_JOBS` and `backupCreate` has **no failure notification path** — its only `notify` is the success one.

**Customer sees:** `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/BackupSchedule.tsx:103-105` renders "Last automatic backup: 2026-07-26 04:00 UTC", refreshed every night.
**Truth:** that timestamp means "a job row was created". vzdump may have failed every night for a month. No alert ever fires, and the schedule is marked satisfied so the retry is a full interval away. Discovered only at restore time, which is the one moment it cannot be fixed.
**Smallest fix:** delete the `lastAutoBackup` write in `backup-schedule.ts` (the in-flight de-dupe at :50-53 already prevents pile-up) and set it in `backupCreate` after the task returns, gated on a storage-content read showing a fresh volid with `size > 0`. Add a failure `notify` in a catch.

### 2. `syncPortForwards` flushes the whole NAT chain, then rebuilds with no verification
`/opt/nxeon/worker/network.ts:28-55` (I read this file in full)

Line 30 does `iptables -t nat -F NXEON_FWD` unconditionally, then rebuilds server-by-server in a loop with **no try/catch, no rollback, and no `-C` read-back**. `exec` is `promisify(execFile)`, so one failed `-A` rejects and aborts the loop — every server after that point has no DNAT rule at all.

**Customer sees:** dashboard lists their SSH port; the `SYNC_FORWARDS` job goes DONE (`index.ts:787` — DONE means only "the last `iptables -A` exited 0").
**Truth:** fleet-wide SSH blackhole, no notification, no ERROR status. `remove()` at `index.ts:401` calls this *after* deleting the server row, so a throw re-queues DELETE, which then dies on "Server not found" and never retries the sync.
**Smallest fix:** build into a scratch chain and swap atomically; at minimum collect per-rule failures instead of aborting, then assert each server's SSH rule with `iptables -t nat -C` and throw listing the servers whose rule is missing.

### 3. Volume delete destroys the disk unverified, then deletes the row and stops billing
`/opt/nxeon/worker/volumes.ts:1279-1305`

The scsi→unused detach *is* gated by `waitForConfig` (:1288-1292). The POST that actually **destroys the disk** (:1296) has no read-back — despite the correct helper sitting four lines above. Secondary: the guard at :1279 is `if (server?.vmid && volume.diskName)`, so a null-server volume skips the Proxmox block entirely and the row is deleted anyway.

**Customer sees:** "Volume deleted", row gone, billing stops.
**Truth:** up to 2000 GB can remain on `vmdata` with no DB row pointing at it — unbillable, unfindable, and counting against capacity for every future sale on that node.
**Smallest fix:** after :1296, `await waitForConfig(conn, vmid, c => !keyForVolid(c, volume.diskName))` and throw if it is still present.

### 4. Mailbox suspend and delete swallow the Mailcow error, then assert the outcome
`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:733-752` and `:704-716`

```
734:  await mcSetMailboxActive(mailbox.address, !suspended).catch((e) => {
735:    console.warn(...);   // swallowed
739:  await db.mailbox.update({ ... data: { status: suspended ? "SUSPENDED" : "ACTIVE" } });
752:  return { ok: true };
```

**Customer sees:** the badge flips to "Suspended" and `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/EmailHosting.tsx:482-484` states **"Sign-in is disabled for this mailbox."**
**Truth:** if Mailcow rejected the call, the mailbox still authenticates and still receives mail. This is a security control reporting success it never obtained — the ex-employee / compromised-account case.
`removeMailbox` is worse in one respect: the Mailcow delete is swallowed (:705-707) and then the **local row is deleted** (:710), so the mailbox keeps receiving mail on Mailcow with no record left to retry from, and the customer believes the data is gone.
**Smallest fix:** both are one line — drop the `.catch`, let it throw, and return `{ error }` before the DB write. `lib/actions-mailbox-settings.ts:419-421` already does exactly this for sieve rules with the comment *"Deliberately do NOT persist: a stored 'forwarding on' that the server is not running is the exact defect this replaces."*

---

## Tier 2 — customer pays for something they did not get

### 5. `RESIZE` never grows the guest filesystem but reports the new disk size
`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:588-609`

`worker/disk-expand.ts:193-281` has the entire rescan → `growpart` → `resize2fs`/`xfs_growfs` machinery. `RESIZE` calls none of it, then notifies "resized to Max — 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM / 160 GB disk".
**Truth:** `df -h /` shows the old size. Unlike DISK_EXPAND — which explicitly refuses to leave a customer "paying for space they can't see" (`disk-expand.ts:45-49`) — RESIZE gives no warning and no manual commands.
**Smallest fix:** call the existing `growGuestFilesystem(server, step)` after the power cycle and reuse `disk-expand.ts:374-387`'s honest one-step-left wording.

### 6. Provision and resize discard the disk-resize UPID
`/opt/nxeon/worker/index.ts:308-311` and `:589-592`

`worker/disk-expand.ts:344-351` proves this endpoint returns a UPID and awaits it. These two call sites throw it away — the 200 only means PVE queued the grow. On provision it runs *before* the start at :315, so the VM boots on whatever size actually landed and a silent failure is invisible forever, with `extraDiskGB` already paid for.

### 7. Databases marked ACTIVE with a one-time password that was never tested
`/opt/nxeon/worker/databases.ts:111-130`

Success is `CREATE`/`ALTER` exiting 0 as root. `/opt/nxeon/worker/apps.ts:495-506` does exactly the missing login probe, with the comment *"the CREATE statement exited 0 is not evidence that it will log in."* The standalone creator never got that fix. Aggravating: `passwordEnc` is nulled at :126 and the password is shown once (`lib/actions-databases.ts:162`) — if it doesn't work, nobody can re-derive it.

### 8. Websites reach ACTIVE / "is live and serving" with zero HTTP verification
`/opt/nxeon/worker/websites.ts:150-171`, plus `reloadNginx` at `:128-132`

None of lines 150/151/158/160 check `.code`; line 150's `|| true` covers the whole `mkdir && chown` chain. `reloadNginx` checks `nginx -t` but discards the result of the actual `systemctl reload nginx || systemctl restart nginx` (:131).

## Tier 3 — false security and privacy claims

### 9. SSL health probe accepts any certificate on :443, including Cloudflare's or a self-signed one
`/opt/nxeon/worker/ssl.ts:501-507` and `:579-599`

The handshake uses `rejectUnauthorized: false` (correct for *observing*) but then only checks name-match and future `notAfter`. It never reads `socket.authorized`/`authorizationError` or the issuer. For a domain behind Cloudflare it captures the **edge** cert, writes ACTIVE, overwrites `expiresAt` with the edge expiry, and clears `lastError` — so the origin's real Let's Encrypt cert is **never renewed** and dies silently.
**Smallest fix:** capture `socket.authorized` in the callback and require it true at :579 before writing ACTIVE / overwriting expiry.

### 10. Renewal reports "renewed" without checking the expiry moved
`/opt/nxeon/worker/ssl.ts:426-435` and `:665-677`

`not yet due for renewal` is explicitly accepted as success; `readObservedExpiry` then reads back the **unchanged** date. The customer gets a notification titled "SSL certificate renewed for example.com — Verified live … valid until <old date>". Nothing was renewed.
**Smallest fix:** when `isRenewal && cert.expiresAt`, require `expiresAt > cert.expiresAt`; otherwise keep the status and set `lastError` instead of notifying success.

### 11. WHOIS privacy is a purely local toggle that renders a green checklist tick
`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-domains-advanced.ts:133-152` → `/opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/domains/[id]/page.tsx:115`

`setWhoisPrivacy` writes `db.domain.update({ data: { whoisPrivacy: enabled } })` and **never contacts the registrar at all**. The returned note is honest, but it sits under a lit toggle, and the setup checklist renders `{ label: "WHOIS privacy on", done: domain.whoisPrivacy }` as a green ✓.
**Truth:** for a transferred-in domain where privacy was never purchased, a customer can tick "WHOIS privacy on" and have their home address remain public. (Mitigating: `registrar.ts:168` sends `privacyEnabled: true` at registration, so Nxeon-registered domains are usually genuinely private.)
**Smallest fix:** make the checklist item read from a registrar `domainInfo` field, or render it as "preference saved — contact support to change on a live domain" rather than a completed step.

### 12. The email-verification gate uses the untrusted system resolver
`/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-email-hosting.ts:5` and `:463-478`

`verifyEmailDomain` — the gate that grants the ability to mint mailboxes on a domain — uses bare `resolveTxt`/`resolveMx` from `node:dns/promises`. It is the **only** remaining consumer of the system resolver in the repo. Meanwhile `lib/mail/deliverability.ts:30-36` has a 25-line comment about exactly this trap and resolves via pinned bootstrap resolvers → the zone's own authoritative nameservers. The trust is inverted: the cosmetic diagnostic is hardened, the security gate is not.
**Smallest fix:** export the authoritative-resolver helper from `deliverability.ts` and use it in `verifyEmailDomain`.
